observationFocus: Ignore top-page UI such as the Level label, level dropdown, Go to Level button, Space to restart text, Login text, and hamburger/menu icon; focus only on the puzzle board below.
Focus on the player, boxes, targets, walls, blocked paths, corridors, and whether a push creates or avoids deadlocks.
Treat the pale beige floor as walkable space and the dark stone pattern as solid wall / non-walkable area.
Treat the pink dots as targets, the orange or brown crates as boxes, and the human sprite as the player.
Describe the player's location relative to the nearest corridor, wall edge, or box cluster instead of narrating the whole scene.
Identify the nearest relevant box and target relationship before proposing the next move.
Before proposing a move, verify the immediate next tile in that direction: if it is a wall or blocked box chain, do not choose that move.
When the board is static and legible, prefer a bounded plan of 2-4 grounded moves instead of a single vague nudge.
Explain progress in concrete puzzle terms: player position, box access, target alignment, and whether a path just opened or closed.
Distinguish between pure player repositioning, opening a route, pushing a box, moving a box closer to a target, and completely failing to move.
Do not treat 'the player moved' as automatically meaning puzzle progress; explain whether that movement created a useful setup.
Do not say only 'keep moving' or 'try moving'; always tie the next move to a specific nearby box, lane, wall, or opening.
notes: You can only push boxes, never pull them.
Avoid pushing boxes into unrecoverable corners.
If the very next tile in the chosen direction is a wall, that move is invalid and should not be selected.
Prefer moves that create visible progress or better positioning over moves that simply bump into walls.
When a short sequence is clearly available, choose it and keep each step grounded in the current board layout.
If a move only repositions the player, say so explicitly; do not overclaim box progress.
If a move changes the board but the exact box relation is still ambiguous, admit that the layout changed but the exact new setup is still resolving.
